target_customer: Lithium-ion battery cell makers and automotive manufacturers
problem: Conventional plastic separator films add cost and manufacturing infrastructure and are a main source of battery fire risk. Nuvola sprays a porous polymer separator directly onto electrodes.
business_model: Technology and materials licensing and coating process for battery manufacturers

founders.name: Janet Hur
founders.background_notes: YC page lists her as cofounder of Nuvola Technology (formerly Millibatt, Inc.).

founders.name: Leland Smith
founders.background_notes: Listed as founder on the YC page. A search snippet says the founders are UCLA PhD materials scientists, not confirmed in an opened source.

technical_complexity.rationale: A direct-deposited separator needs materials science, roll-to-roll process integration and safety validation at battery makers.

defensibility.rationale: The company's site says nine global patents issued since 2018, though adoption by cell makers depends on cost and qualification cycles.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent acquisition or copy found. A 2023 analyst comment quoted in coverage cautioned that cost increases for makers would block adoption.

market_need_then: Battery fires and EV growth made safety and cost key concerns, but sources dated 2017 on separator demand were not found. In 2022 the company won an LG Energy Solution battery challenge per a 2023 press release snippet.

identity.logo: Teal and white logo per the company site
identity.visual_style: Technical, product-led with SafeCoat as the lead product brand

brand_strength.rationale: Little brand-level press. Coverage focuses on the product, and the company changed its name from Millibatt.

outcome_analysis: Nuvola remains active with about four people on the YC page and has publicized safety tests and sampling with battery makers, but I found no disclosed priced funding round or named commercial customer. The slow qualification cycles in battery manufacturing and the long gap since 2017 suggest a stalled-but-alive technology company, though public facts are thin.
notes: Aggregators (CB Insights, FounderNest) show about $120K over 3 rounds with Q Venture Partners, with conflicting dates in 2017; kept out of rounds as unverified and probably the YC deal. Competitor list is empty because the 2017 competitor article could not be opened (HTTP 403). The 2023 Business Wire release and the 2025 nail penetration release could not be fetched, so details come from search summaries. Coeur Renewables backing came from one search summary and is unverified. Completeness pass: one seed round rests on a single database (CB Insights, 1 Jun 2017; FounderNest says 20 Mar 2017). CB Insights total is about $120K over 3 rounds, with Pegasus Tech Ventures, YC and Strong Ventures also listed as investors but per-round amounts not given. Seedtable lists no rounds.
